lesson: Approval and write effects: a plan may hold as many approval-requiring effects as the work needs, provided each of those tasks has a literal input. Every one of their exact request hashes is computed from the plan before anything runs, the operator grants the set, and the run completes in a single pass without re-attempting any task, so no completed write is ever repeated. Splitting such work into one effect per plan is not a safety measure and costs a model call per effect. What remains refused is several approval-requiring effects where one takes its input from another task's output: that request cannot exist until the earlier effect has already happened, so give the gated tasks literal inputs or propose the dependent effect as its own plan. Staging a long job across separate plans is still right when it must survive the process ending between stages, but that is a durability reason, not an approval-count one.
